thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: inference-api (us-west-2) high tail latency (p95 > 1.2s) — paging oncall team now. Incident ID: INC-20260315-27

alex_m: on it. seeing a sustained rise in GPU queue length and KV cache miss rate. spikes started ~ 10:05 PDT. no obvious deploys in last 30m.

dave_r: can you share the exact metrics? attaching quick grafana links if helpful: https://grafana.redwood.io/d/ops/paging-overview?panelId=7

alex_m: sure — p95 tokens/sec queue: 2.4x baseline, kv_cache_hit drops from 0.92 -> 0.63. also seeing per-model queue growth on rtx-8000 pool.

elena_p: customer impact check: internal telemetry shows 12 customer requests timed out between 10:12-10:28 in the hosted API. hitting SLA thresholds for a handful of business-critical customers. notifying CS.

dave_r: quick mitigation idea: throttle large-batch jobs and fall back to quantized model variant for low-priority routes. can we flip routing policy to prefer dedicated pool where possible?

alex_m: doing the following now: 1) increase autoscaler min nodes for rtx-8000 pool by +2 (expected to add capacity in ~3m). 2) apply emergency routing rule to send non-critical workspace traffic to dedicated-region fallback. 3) enable prefix KV cache warm-up for most frequent sessions.

elena_p: good. also propose we adjust paging thresholds post-incident — current paging rule triggers on host cpu_util > 70% for 3m which is noisy for short spikes. I'd like to change to cpu_util > 85% for 5m and add a secondary alert on sustained queue_length > 100 for 2m.

dave_r: agree on multi-signal rule. here's a draft snippet to update the alert (will open PR after):
```yaml
alert: inference_high_latency
expr: (cpu_utilization > 0.85 and cpu_utilization > cpu_utilization:avg_over_5m) or (queue_length > 100)
for: 2m
labels:
  severity: critical
annotations:
  runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/paging_playbook
```

alex_m: applied the autoscaler bump, new nodes are joining. routing flip is in progress (low-priority routes only). KV warm-up script triggered. seeing immediate drop in queue growth. p95 trending back down.

incident-bot: Update: INC-20260315-27 status -> mitigated (partial). alerting suppressed via temporary silences.

elena_p: action items for postmortem/runbook: 1) adopt the new multi-signal alert rule (owner: dave_r) 2) create a dedicated dashboard for queue_length by model and pool (owner: elena_p) 3) add an escalation step to the runbook to adjust routing policy before paging (owner: alex_m) 4) add an opt-in quiet-hours policy for non-prod paging (owner: sarah_ops).

dave_r: opened PR with alert change and tests: https://git.internal.redwood/repo/alerts/pulls/412 — includes CI lint and links to runbook. cc @elena_p for dashboard panels.

elena_p: creating dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.io/d/new/paging-by-model — will add annotations for this incident and include panels for kv_cache_hit, queue_length, p95_latency, and autoscaler events.

sarah_ops: taking handoff for night rotation in 20m. summary for next oncall: mitigations applied (autoscaler +2, routing flip for non-prod, KV warmup), partial mitigation confirmed, running monitoring for 30m. key links: runbook https://redwood.internal/runbooks/paging_playbook, alert PR https://git.internal.redwood/repo/alerts/pulls/412, dashboard https://grafana.redwood.io/d/new/paging-by-model. escalate to eng-sre if we see p95 > 1s for more than 10m.

alex_m: note for runbook update — add a short checklist and exact CLI steps to do routing flip and to confirm which route ids are safe to reroute. I'll add a small demo snippet to the runbook.

incident-bot: INC-20260315-27 resolved -> monitoring. Incident severity downgraded to SEV-3 for postmortem.

sarah_ops: acknowledged. I'll file the post-incident ticket and schedule a 30m review tomorrow. owners: dave_r (alerts), elena_p (dashboard), alex_m (runbook routing section), sarah_ops (quiet-hours policy). will ping owners in the ticket. :white_check_mark:

alex_m: added quick runbook note (internal link): https://redwood.internal/runbooks/paging_playbook#routing-flip — please verify and I'll PR a more formal edit.

dave_r: final note — for noise reduction, also suggest adding a 10m rate limit on alerting for identical signatures and require both cpu or queue signals before paging. low-risk change but reduces pagerstorms.

sarah_ops: agreed. leaving a silence window for non-prod alerts for the night and will re-evaluate thresholds in the morning. handoff complete.
